title: Scaling Laws for Neural Language Models
authors: J. Kaplan, S. McCandlish, T. Henighan, et al. (10 authors)
before: Bigger models were known to be better, but nobody could say how much better in advance.
problem: Without a predictable relationship, scale-up is a gamble rather than an investment.
breakthrough: Loss falls as a smooth power law in parameters, data and compute, across seven orders of magnitude.
why: It converted scale from a hunch into a budgeting exercise, and directly motivated GPT-3.
next: GPT-3 was the demonstration; Chinchilla corrected the allocation two years later.
inherits: The practice of forecasting a model's loss before training it.
